title.narrative: Maintaining the integrity of globally significant intact tropical forest landscapes in the Gulf Province and Western Province of Papua New Guinea

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The project has a strong focus on improving rural livelihoods through forest, protected area, fisheries and farm management including by generating livelihood benefits through value chains, markets, and sustainable financing. Prioritized Groups - Customary landowners and community stakeholders with a focus on women and youth Pillar 1: Employment-creation and enterprise-development · Participatory analyses with vulnerable groups on employment issues related to PA access, natural resource use, farms and forests. · Consultation with relevant groups, and vetting of PA management priorities and solutions, for discussion. · Support women and men small-scale farm and forest producers in accessing: o Defining natural resource use agreements, collaborative management and benefit sharing. (including zonation and participatory demarcation, sustainability parameters and sustainable off take of NTFPs, etc). o Fair markets and sustainable value chains o Training, financial services, and other productive assets · Provide Market Analysis and Development training. · Implement training for government agencies and project partners to enable uptake of participatory, collaborative managementapproaches with communities. Pillar 2: Social protection · Review and share institutional innovations and good practices of organized collective action Pillar 3: Standards and rights at work · Support socially responsible agricultural and forest production underscoring the project’s main BD aims, and to reduce gender and age-based discrimination. · Promote compliance with and suggest improvements to national policies, including labor legislation. · Address constraints of women, youth, and other specific groups workers in getting organized Pillar 4: Governance and social dialogue · Promote inclusive participation of local people, particularly women. · Support customary landowners and community stakeholders to strengthen the project’s conservation aims and networks of producers and workers. · Build capacity of customary landowners and community stakeholders to organize into legalized associations and women to undertake leading positions. · Share knowledge on project collaborative management, natural resource use agreements, benefit sharing and climate-resilient forest and agricultural management.
To maintain the integrity of globally significant intact tropical forest landscapes in Gulf Province and Western Province of Papua New Guinea.
